description: The image illustrates five distinct distribution shapes or structural patterns using a series of small, horizontally arranged bar charts. The charts lack explicit vertical axis lines, tick marks, or numerical scales, relying on a shared horizontal baseline where the vertical height of the bars indicates an unlabeled relative value. The horizontal axis for each individual chart consists of an unlabeled sequence of four adjacent bins or categories. Every chart contains four light green bars with black outlines. The first chart, which has a grayed-out rectangular box instead of a text label beneath it, shows bars strictly increasing in height from left to right, with the shortest bar on the far left and the tallest on the far right. The second chart, labeled "Uniform", displays four bars of identical height. The third chart, labeled "Decreasing", shows bars strictly decreasing in height from left to right, starting with the tallest bar and ending with the shortest. The fourth chart, labeled "Spindle", features two short outer bars and two taller, equal-height inner bars. The fifth chart, labeled "Bottleneck", displays two tall, equal-height outer bars and two shorter, equal-height inner bars. The charts are not sorted by a specific numerical value but are presented sequentially to demonstrate different geometric configurations.
